@sketch
Feature: Coincident






  @needs_fixture
  Scenario: coincident-06 Cancel then constrain a fresh point to a line
    Given the fixture contains a free point and two overlapping collinear line segments
    When the user invoke Coincident and select only the point
    Then the command requests a second curve or point
    When the user press Escape
    Then Ready returns without visible point movement
    When the user invoke Coincident, select the point, then click once where the line interiors overlap
    Then the point moves onto the supporting line and a coincidence marker appears
    And the command requests the first curve or point again
    When the user press Escape then Ctrl+Z
    Then the original visible point position returns
    When the user press Ctrl+Y
    Then the constrained position returns
    When the user measure the point and one of the overlapping lines
    Then Measure identifies a Point and a Curve of length 17.120 mm
    And the minimum distance is 0.000 mm at displayed precision
    And the displayed point position is (0.000, -15.859, 37.529) mm
    And the maximum distance is 23.939 mm

  @needs_fixture
  Scenario: Compare a constrained point with the measured overlapping line span
    Given the recorded point-to-line coincidence is retained
    And the constrained point's displayed position is (0.000, -15.859, 37.529) mm
    When the user use Measure to select the two recorded point locations at the line span
    Then their displayed Point positions are (0.000, -19.874, 32.017) and (0.000, -29.952, 18.178) mm
    And their separation is 17.120 mm
    And the earlier selected Curve also measured 17.120 mm
    And interpreting those measured points as endpoints, a projection of the constrained point falls beyond the first end of the span

  @needs_fixture
  Scenario: coincident-07 Constrain two standalone points and inspect history
    Given two separate standalone points
    When the user invoke Coincident and select the upper-left point
    Then the prompt requests a second curve or point
    When the user select the lower-right point
    Then it moves onto the first point and a coincidence marker appears there
    And the prompt returns to the first curve or point
    When the user press Escape
    Then the placement remains
    When the user undo the relation
    Then both points appear separately again
    When the user redo the relation
    Then their shared visible position returns

  @needs_fixture
  Scenario: coincident-08 Reject coincidence between separately fixed points
    Given an isolated pair of separated points
    When the user invoke Fix and select each point
    Then lock glyphs appear beside both points
    When the user exit Fix and invoke Coincident
    And the user select the first point followed by the second
    Then Create Constraint reports Cannot constrain or dimension reference or fixed geometry
    And both points remain separate
    When the user click Cancel in the feedback window
    Then Coincident returns to its first-selection prompt
    When the user press Escape
    Then the MCAD Software returns to Ready and the separate points remain

  @needs_fixture
  Scenario: coincident-09 Join endpoints of separate oblique segments
    Given two separate oblique segments in the recorded endpoint-join fixture
    When the user invoke Coincident
    And the user select the first segment end followed by the second segment start
    Then the endpoints meet at a new shared visible location
    And both segments change their visible extent or placement
    And the prompt returns to first curve or point
    When the user press Escape
    Then the joined geometry remains
    When the user press F8
    Then constraint markers are displayed including the marker at the joint

  @needs_fixture
  Scenario: coincident-10 Inspect the shared point context without removing geometry
    Given the joined line endpoints and visible constraints
    When the user right-click the joint
    Then a Point context menu opens with Repeat Coincident and general point commands
    And marking-menu Delete is disabled
    When the user press Escape
    Then the menu closes
    When the user select the joint point and right-click it again
    Then the point context menu appears without an identified constraint-removal command
    When the user press Escape
    Then the menu closes and both joined segments remain

  @needs_fixture
  Scenario: coincident-11 Remove a segment endpoint relation and inspect history
    Given the joined line endpoints and visible constraints
    When the user right-click the first segment interior
    Then the menu includes Delete Coincident Constraint
    When the user choose that command
    Then the joint marker disappears and both lines retain their positions
    When the user move only the first segment using its start as base point
    Then it separates from the second segment which remains in place
    And no constraint-relaxation or conflict dialog appears
    When the user undo the movement
    Then the endpoints overlap visually without the joint marker
    When the user undo the deletion
    Then the joint marker returns
    When the user redo the deletion
    Then the marker disappears without moving either line
    When the user redo the movement
    Then the first segment separates again

  @needs_fixture
  Scenario: Move a free point to a fixed circle center
    Given a free sketch point and a fixed circle with a separate center
    When the user invoke Coincident and select the free point
    Then the command requests a second curve or point
    When the user select the fixed circle center
    Then the free point moves onto the center
    And the command requests its first curve or point again
    When the user press Escape
    Then the first-selection prompt is still displayed in the recorded state
    When the user press Escape again
    Then the sketch returns to Ready
    When the user undo the relation
    Then the free point returns to its earlier position
    When the user redo the relation
    Then the free point returns to the fixed circle center
